_schema.items: Array of { id, content (raw memory text), expected_category (preference|fact|pattern|decision|outcome), acceptable_entities (array of correct entity strings/aliases — a normalized match against any counts), confidence_band ([min,max] optional plausible confidence range) }.
_schema.design: Built to expose where the rule-based extractor is weak and the LLM should help: (1) IMPLICIT-category items with no trigger keyword from rules.js's CATEGORY_SIGNALS (rules default these to 'fact'); (2) entities NOT in rules.js's TECH_KEYWORDS (product/SaaS/domain names) where the rule extractor returns null or a generic token; (3) a few genuinely ambiguous items (intended label documented in bench/README.md); (4) a spread across all five categories.

ambiguous.x16: decision vs preference — phrased as a preference but carries a rationale ('isn't worth it'); labeled decision.
ambiguous.x22: preference vs fact — opinion stated flatly; labeled preference.
ambiguous.x48: pattern vs preference — a recurring practice stated as a rule; labeled pattern.

items.content: The production database is PostgreSQL 15.
The API runs on Node.js 20 using native ESM modules.
Redis handles caching and rate limiting.
Error tracking for frontend and backend goes through Sentry.
The team tracks issues in Linear.
Application metrics are shipped to Datadog.
User authentication is handled by Clerk.
The CDN and WAF sit in front of the app on Cloudflare.
Background jobs run on a Temporal cluster.
Domain events flow through a Kafka topic.
Data warehouse is Snowflake.
Warehouse transformations are managed with dbt.
Infrastructure is provisioned with Terraform.
Transactional email goes out through Resend.
Feature flags are managed in PostHog.
We'll standardize on Tailwind; maintaining a bespoke CSS bundle isn't worth it.
We chose PostgreSQL over MongoDB for the billing service because transactions need ACID guarantees.
Switched from Webpack to Vite to cut local dev startup time.
We migrated from npm to pnpm for faster CI installs.
Postgres it is for billing — the numbers have to stay atomic.
Going with Stripe for payments; their API docs are the best around.
Routing internal calls over REST; GraphQL is overkill there.
I prefer Fastify over Express for Node.js APIs.
Avoid global state in React components.
I like small, frequently shipped pull requests.
Honestly, Vim keybindings everywhere or I'm miserable.
Prefer Playwright over Cypress for end-to-end tests now.
We typically deploy to production on Fridays.
Every time CI goes red, merges are blocked.
Usually we squash-merge feature branches.
Database migrations run automatically when a service boots.
Standup is async in a thread, not a meeting.
Each release, the changelog is generated from conventional commits.
Moving session storage to Redis fixed the random logouts under load.
The Vite switch improved cold dev-server start dramatically.
Adding request-id tracing solved most of our triage pain.
After we added the read-through cache, p99 latency dropped from 800ms to 90ms.
pnpm took our CI install from about 90 seconds to 25.
Once we sharded the orders table, the deadlocks stopped.
The design files live in Figma.
We'll route payments through Stripe Billing; building our own dunning is a waste of time.
API rate limiting is 100 requests per minute per key.
Secrets live in AWS Secrets Manager, never in a committed .env.
The mobile app is built with React Native.
Standardized on Vitest after Jest got too slow for our suite.
Postgres connection pooling is done with PgBouncer.
The on-call rotation handed off to Grafana OnCall last quarter.
We pin exact dependency versions and review every bump.
